title: Sort markdown tables on GitHub
question: How do I sort a table in a GitHub README by a column?
answer: GitHub does not let you sort tables in rendered markdown; they show in the order the author wrote them. The usermods script on this page makes every column header in a README or markdown file table clickable: one click sorts the rows by that column, a second click reverses the order, and an arrow marks the sorted column. Numbers sort by value, so 9.x comes before 10.x. Without an extension, copying the table into a spreadsheet is the usual way.
prompt: Let me click the column headers of tables in GitHub READMEs to sort them.
details:
The script sorts the table's rows in the page; it does not change the file. Empty cells and cells holding only a dash stay at the bottom in both directions. Links inside a header still work as links.

It works on any rendered markdown on github.com, including issue and pull request comments and wiki pages; the check covers a README.

alternatives.title: Copy into a spreadsheet
alternatives.body: Select the table, copy it and paste it into Google Sheets, Numbers or Excel, which keep the columns and can sort them.

alternatives.title: Sortable Tables for GitHub
alternatives.body: The Sortable Tables for GitHub extension for Chrome does the same.

check.actions: const t = [...document.querySelectorAll('article.markdown-body table')].find((t) => t.tBodies[0] && t.tBodies[0].rows.length >= 20); window.__t = t; window.__before = t && [...t.tBodies[0].rows].map((r) => r.cells[6].textContent.trim()); const th = t && [...t.tHead.rows[0].cells].find((c) => c.textContent.trim() === 'End-of-life'); th && th.click();
check.baseline: (() => { const t = window.__t; if (!t || !t.checkVisibility()) return false; const now = [...t.tBodies[0].rows].map((r) => r.cells[6].textContent.trim()); const named = now.filter((s) => s && s !== '-'); const sorted = [...named].sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b)); return now.length >= 20 && now.join() === window.__before.join() && named.join() !== sorted.join(); })()
check.expect: (() => { const t = window.__t; const th = [...t.tHead.rows[0].cells].find((c) => c.textContent.trim() === 'End-of-life'); const now = [...t.tBodies[0].rows].map((r) => r.cells[6].textContent.trim()); const named = now.filter((s) => s && s !== '-'); const sorted = [...named].sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b)); const firstEmpty = now.findIndex((s) => !s || s === '-'); const emptiesLast = firstEmpty === -1 || now.slice(firstEmpty).every((s) => !s || s === '-'); return th.getAttribute('aria-sort') === 'ascending' && now.length === window.__before.length && named.length >= 10 && named.join() === sorted.join() && emptiesLast; })()
check.intact: (() => { const t = window.__t; const rows = [...t.tBodies[0].rows].filter((r) => r.checkVisibility()); return rows.length >= 20 && rows.every((r) => r.cells.length === t.tHead.rows[0].cells.length) && document.querySelectorAll('article.markdown-body table').length >= 3; })()
